Borrowed from Spanish cebiche, of uncertain origin; see that entry for more. Cf. escabeche.
Anglicised spelling of Serbo-Croatian ćevapčići (see ћевап).
Borrowed from Serbo-Croatian ćevapi / ћевапи, from Ottoman Turkish كباب (kebâp), from Arabic كَبَاب (kabāb) or Persian کباب (kabâb, “fried meat”). Doublet of kebab.
q: The chef, Andreas Klironomos, is of Greek heritage, but he turns out gibanica (cheese in phyllo) and ćevapi (grilled minced meat).
